sprint: Sheet Extractor inside Image Studio — three new tools, built by reusing the standalone tool's already-verified engines rather than reimplementing them. Cut Out Objects runs extractSheet on the current picture and shows a grid of everything it found: tap one cutout to replace the picture, or Use All to send every cutout back to the caller at once. Outline and Colour Fill are TileEditor's own outline and bucketFill, wired to the existing snapshot-backed undo. Sheet and Scan detection are both offered, with the render axis (ink fill on/off) kept independent of the detection axis exactly as the standalone tool separates them.
task:
REUSE, NOT REIMPLEMENTATION: index.html now loads tools/sheet-extractor/js/extractor.js and js/tileEditor.js directly, so Image Studio calls the same extractSheet and TileEditor the standalone tool's own 47/32/12/38-assertion suites already cover. No detection, tracing, ink-fill, outline or bucket-fill logic was copied into js/pictureStudio.js.

THE ONE NEW CONTRACT: PictureStudio.open(src, opts) gains an OPTIONAL opts.onApplyMany(dataUrls). Only js/contextPanel.js's Add Something -> Photo call site opts in; the other ten open() call sites pass only onApply and are completely unaffected. Use All reads each cutout from its own PngEncoder blob via FileReader rather than re-drawing through a canvas, because canvas export corrupts RGB at partial alpha (premultiplied backing store) — the exact reason the standalone tool keeps <canvas> out of its write path in the first place.

ONE TEST BUG, fixed properly and never weakened: the suite's seen() helper checked classList.contains('hidden') on the INPUT, but the app toggles hidden on the row WRAPPER, so seen() always returned true and four B assertions passed for the wrong reason. Rewritten to el.offsetParent !== null — real rendered visibility, which additionally proves the .picture-studio-subpanel-row.hidden{display:none} rule genuinely exists (css/style.css:4908). That matters because this codebase has no global .hidden utility and has shipped a bug of exactly that class before (.text-empty). B: 5/9 -> 9/9.

FOUR GENUINE APP BUGS, each found by instrumenting or reading the real code path rather than guessing:
1. _runExtract read (res && res.objects) but extractSheet resolves { items: [...] }, so the grid was always empty and C2 timed out.
2. PngEncoder was never loaded in Studio even though extractor.js calls it at two sites. After fixing #1 the extraction still failed; a six-probe diagnostic with page.on('pageerror') surfaced "ReferenceError: PngEncoder is not defined", which _runExtract's own .catch had been converting into the friendly "Couldn't find anything this time." One script tag fixed it. C: 1/7 -> 7/7.
3. _hide() left _workingBuffer stale. _workingBuffer and _bgRemovedImg are a matched pair — _ensureWorkingBuffer mints them together and _syncCanvasFromBuffer needs both — and the other two reset sites (_undoBgRemoval and "Yes, start over") correctly null the pair. _hide() nulled only _bgRemovedImg, so on a RE-OPEN _ensureWorkingBuffer early-returned on the stale buffer and never re-minted the canvas: every pixel tool (extract, crop, outline, fill, erase) silently operated on the PREVIOUS picture's pixels and painted nothing. Broader than extract, and the reason D2 timed out. Fixed by nulling the pair plus the five companion fields that describe the picture that just went away, so a re-open can never offer an Undo Trim that would restore a different picture.
4. _applyAllExtracted read _onApplyMany AFTER _hide() had nulled it, so Use All threw "not a function" into a silent catch and dropped every cutout on the floor. _hide() nulls _onApplyMany but not _onApply, which is exactly why the single-picture path never hit this. Fixed by capturing the callback before teardown. D3 now passes.

Verified 46/46, zero failures, sections A-H: A engines reachable and the three tiles present; B the two detection modes with their own field sets (both sensitivity sliders carry the identical label, so they are told apart by range — sheet 6-90, scan 4-60 — never by label text); C a real extraction finding both fixture objects and rendering two tiles; D tapping a tile replaces the picture and Use All returns both cutouts through onApplyMany; E outline grows the shape with working undo; F bucket fill applied by tapping the canvas; G contextual tile collapse and the back button; H zero page errors.

Full regression: both goldenBuild suites PASS, bg_default 12/12, image_studio_draw 26/26, crop_fix 23/23, photo_via_studio 8/8, fa_replace_everywhere 22/22. renderer/slideRenderer.js is untouched, so the Museum Gallery hashes are not the gate for this ship. Cache-bust ?v=0358 -> ?v=0359 across all 59 tags.
